dated_ledger.recorded_statement: For nondegenerate continuous iid planar passage-time laws in the usual positive-speed regime, determine whether a bi-infinite geodesic exists.
dated_ledger.status: attempted_unsolved as recorded 2026-09-07; not evidence of current openness

original_problem_source.citation: Auffinger, Damron, Hanson, 50 years of first-passage percolation, Question 31
original_problem_source.locator: PDF page 86 (zero-based page 85), section 4.5; the local bundle's 'PDF p.98' locator does not match this PDF edition
original_problem_source.scope_note: The survey asks the broader geodesic-line question; P0117 is its planar iid specialization. The question text itself supplies no moment hypothesis.

older_partial_theorem.citation: Damron and Hanson, Bigeodesics in first-passage percolation, arXiv:1512.00804v2 (2016)
older_partial_theorem.content: No bigeodesic with an end in a fixed deterministic direction under differentiability of the shape boundary; the fixed-direction quantifier does not cover an environment-selected random direction.

new_primary_preprint.citation: OpenAI, No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation, dated 2026-09-24, Theorem 1.1
new_primary_preprint.claimed_statement: For iid nonnegative nonatomic nearest-neighbor edge weights on Z^2 with E[min(X1,X2,X3,X4)^2] < infinity, almost surely no doubly infinite path has every finite segment geodesic. The assertion is simultaneous over all paths and assumes no limit-shape regularity.
new_primary_preprint.evidence: PDF Theorem 1.1 and introduction, extracted text lines 26-43
new_primary_preprint.assessment: A direct primary-source claim of a solution for the moment class, not an independently validated proof. It does not claim the moment-free case. Section 7.4's fixed-M/fixed-neighborhood limit and Proposition 7.6's final Busemann-detour deduction were checked only conditional on upstream lemmas.
